anchor: Country-level signature data: demographics (% foreign-born, % foreign-owned SMBs), 3 signature sectors that characterise the country (banks, asset management, and farms excluded as too generic), 6 cultural spectrum scores (1-10 low-left/high-right), and 5 government-and-institutions scores (0-10, higher = better for business). Used by CitySignaturePanel as the fallback when a city has no explicit override. Anchored to 2024-2025 indices: Transparency International CPI, World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators, World Justice Project Rule of Law Index, WIPO Global Innovation Index, Hofstede national-culture dimensions, GLOBE study, UN DESA migrant stock, WTO trade statistics. Convention: 'corruption_rejection' is renamed (was acceptance_of_corruption) so every spectrum reads low-left / high-right uniformly.

convention.demographics: foreign_born_pct = UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024 share. foreign_owned_pct = approximate share of SMBs with at least one foreign owner, from WB Enterprise Surveys + OECD FDI penetration.
convention.signature_sectors: Three industries that characterise the country vs comparable peers. Banks, asset management, and farms (agriculture, livestock, aquaculture) are excluded as too generic.

government.low_bribery: 0 = widespread, 10 = bribery rare (anchored to Transparency International CPI 2024)
government.task_efficiency: 0 = nothing works, 10 = things get done (anchored to WGI Government Effectiveness)
government.time_efficiency: 0 = months for any permit, 10 = same-day filing (anchored to B-Ready 2024)
government.judicial_impartiality: 0 = courts captured, 10 = fully impartial (anchored to WJP Rule of Law Index)

convention.excluded_sectors_note: Banks, asset management firms, and farms (agriculture, livestock, aquaculture) are excluded from signature sectors because every economy has them and they don't distinguish one country from another in a useful way. London insurance is an explicit exception because the city is the global hub.
